newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs seen having positive bias in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: JGBs seen having positive bias in Tokyo.

text.p: The key June 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract is expected to have a slight upward bias on Friday, carrying over firm sentiment from Thursday's trade, traders said.

"I think JGBs have confirmed the (short-term) bottom during Thursday's trade and on LIFFE overnight, and I believe they will begin exploring the upside today," said a trader for a city bank's securities unit.
Movements are likely to be limited, however, ahead of the release of key U.S. jobs data and a Japanese national holiday on Monday, traders said.
"One key for the market is whether investors begin buying today, but they will probably adopt a cautious stance," the trader for a city bank's securities unit said.
JGBs may revert to an upward trend next week if the June ends Friday's trade at above 125.00, but may falter if the yen slides further, said a trader for a trust bank's securities unit.

"Some say the JGB market has already factored in a rise in the dollar to 130 yen, but if the dollar breaks above 127 yen, I think the speed of its rise may surprise the market, and lead to selling of JGBs," he said.
